text:
olivia: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a modular seed-swap flow for on-prem airgap upgrades. Goal: swap just the changed model/component shards instead of full seed images, with built-in backpressure and operator UX for partial/resumable swaps. link: https://rfd/repo/seed-swap-proposal

sam: Nice. How do you reason about mixed-state during swap? i.e., some nodes have new shards, others old — are we accepting mixed model traffic?

olivia: We avoid mixed-serving by making activation a separate two-phase step: stage -> verify -> activate. During stage we write blobs and verify signatures; revertible. Only after a quorum of nodes hit 'staged' can operator trigger activate cluster-wide. Until activate, runtime continues serving pinned version.

devon: Backpressure: what signals do we use to stop pulling more chunks? disk pressure? saturating network? We need a simple heuristic for onprem agents.

olivia: Plan: agents expose per-node health metrics: available-disk, cpu-load, inbound-bytes. Coordinator uses moving-window rates. If more than 25% of staging nodes report low-disk or active transfers > threshold, we pause new downstream pulls and retry with exponential backoff.

clair: Oncall concern: partial stage failures must be clear in console and ops CLI. We should avoid silent retries that look like "done" but left partial applies.

olivia: Agreed. UX: CLI will have `redwood seed-swap status --node <id>` and console shows per-node state (idle/staging/failed/staged/activating/active). Failures surface with suggested remediation (retry, remove-node, force-rollback).

ben: Product question: operator wants a dry-run + cost estimate (bytes to transfer) before starting. Can we provide that from manifests?

olivia: Yes — manifests include per-component checksums + compressed-size. Coordinator can compute diff and estimate bytes and an optimistic transfer time given per-node bandwidth sample. CLI `--dry-run` prints a concise summary.

sam: What about idempotency and resume? We need deterministic chunk ids and a resume token to avoid double-apply.

olivia: Each chunk has (manifest-id, component-id, offset, sha256). Agent stores a resume-token: md5(manifest-id + node-id + highest-applied-offset). Coordinator passes token on resume. Apply is idempotent because we write chunks to temporary path and verify sha before swapping into final location.

devon: How do we enforce activation safety so models aren't partially active? Can we gate by a quorum and TTL?

olivia: Activation policy: quorum (configurable percent, default 100% for production) + activation-window TTL (e.g., 10m). If quorum isn't reached before TTL, we mark the swap as degraded and open manual remediation. There is also an automatic fallback option for non-critical components: roll-forward best-effort.

clair: What about rollback costs? If activation fails we might need to revert many nodes. Large clusters mean expensive network ops. Need a compact rollback plan.

olivia: Rollback options: 1) fast-swap: keep previous artifacts locally (delta-aware), swap back pointers — minimal transfer. 2) full-rollback: stream previous artifacts if not cached. We plan to cache previous active artifacts for N hours (configurable) to enable cheap rollback.

ben: Observability: what metrics/dashboards should we add so product + support can triage?

olivia: Minimum metrics: per-swap bytes-transferred, per-node apply-latency, stage-success-rate, activation-quorum-progress, resume-counts, rollback-counts. Alerts: stage-failure-rate > 5% in 15m, activation-timeout, high-resume-counts for same swap.

devon: Operator CLI examples? People like concrete ones.

olivia: Proposed snippets:```bash
# estimate
redwood seed-swap apply --manifest /tmp/manifest.yaml --dry-run
# start swap with 50% quorum and keep rollback cache for 2h
redwood seed-swap apply --manifest m.yaml --quorum 50 --rollback-cache 2h
# resume a failed swap
redwood seed-swap resume --swap-id 2026-05-14-17 --token <resume-token>
```

clair: Nice. Also add an explicit `--force-activate` only for emergency ops and gated by RBAC audit logs.

olivia: Yes — force flags require approver + reason and generate an audit event.

sam: Airgap nuance: many customers have intermediary bastions with limited storage. How do we handle seed-chunk staging if intermediary can't hold all chunks?

olivia: We support streaming-forward mode: the bastion streams chunks to target nodes without persisting locally (zero-disk mode). We then rely on the target nodes to write and verify. This reduces bastion footprint but relies on stable network. Option exposed as `--streaming-proxy` with backpressure thresholds.

devon: Security: signature verification + signer rotation? older manifests might use older keys. Need signing-policy.

olivia: Manifest includes signer metadata and key-id. Agent verifier fetches key from local keyring (or HSM). If key not found, operator must install or use escrow mechanism. We plan to support key-rotation cross-sigs: new manifest contains both new and previous sig to allow smooth rotation.

ben: Any big tradeoffs we should call out in the RFC?

olivia: Yes — tradeoffs: increased complexity in coordinator + UI vs transfer savings; slower, more complex resume logic vs better bandwidth usage; caching previous artifacts increases disk usage but reduces rollback cost. Also streaming-proxy reduces bastion disk but increases fragility. We'll call these out and propose sane defaults.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Seed-swap RFC draft published by olivia at 2026-05-14 17:23 UTC — link: https://rfd/repo/seed-swap-proposal/draft

sam: Next steps: I'll sketch the coordinator state machine and a small PoC for streaming-proxy. Who wants to pair on agent resume semantics?

olivia: I can pair with you tomorrow. I'll add state diagrams to the RFC and a sample manifest schema. Thanks all :thumbsup:

clair: Please add runbooks for the common failure modes (verify failure, partial-stage, activation-timeout). oncall needs clear steps.

olivia: Will do — adding runbooks + CLI playbook entries to the RFC.
